title: zima.com, 1996 and 2017
lede: Zima had a website unusually early. These are screenshots of pages saved by the Internet Archive’s Wayback Machine, stored as images; click one to open the original capture. The earliest captures of zima.com are from October 1996.[^33]

captures.label: Home
captures.title: “Adult humanz only”
captures.text: Three links: re:zima, the fridge and write to us. The copyright line reads “1995, 1996 Zima Beverage Company.”

captures.label: The fridge
captures.title: The fridge
captures.text: A clickable refrigerator leading to icons, diversions and sound files. “Close the fridge door when you leave. Your Roommate will have a fit.”

captures.label: re:zima
captures.title: The FAQ
captures.text: Sixteen questions, including “Does Zima Clearmalt show up on a breathalyzer?” and “Who owns Zima Beverage Company?”

captures.label: The return
captures.title: “Are you like, supposed to be here?”
captures.text: The age gate of the limited-release site, in deliberately dated 1990s web style. The footer reads “©2017 Zima Beverage Co., La Crosse, WI.”

snips.text: “Zima was initially introduced in three test markets in September, 1992 and was rolled out nationwide in February, 1994.”
“Zima registers on a breathalyzer like any other alcohol beverage. The notion that it doesn't is just a rumor.”
“Zima has about the same alcohol content as a premium beer ... 3.7% by weight (4.6% by volume).” **148 calories** per 12 ounces.
“Zima Beverage Company is an operating unit of Coors Brewing Company, located in Memphis, TN.”
“Contrary to the ol' rumor mill, there is no Vodka or grain alcohol in Zima.”

note: Screenshots of Internet Archive captures, saved as images. The 2018 “Zima Z2K” site was also archived but its captures no longer render, so it is not shown; Westword quoted its warning that “The end of ZIMA is near…again.”[^27]
